notes: Seeded per BACR category index i, the same rule taiw.json uses:
current = 1 + 0.5i,  desired = min(5, current + [0.5, 1.2, 1.8, 2.5][i % 4]),
gap = desired - current.
overallScore is the mean of the SCORED categories, one decimal:
22 / 8 = 2.75 -> 2.8. That is also what MaturityAssessment.tsx computes, since
it filters `current > 0` before averaging.
answeredCategories === totalCategories so isDraft is false. The DRAFT
watermark path is therefore NOT covered - see README.
THE NINTH CATEGORY IS GONE. This block carried a ninth row, "Overall
Assessment" (5 / 5 / 0). bacrQuestions.json holds 804 questions across EIGHT
distinct categories and none of them is "Overall Assessment", so no client
answer can ever produce that row. A perfect 5.0 averaged in as if it were a
real category put 27 / 9 = 3.0 on the cover where the eight measured
categories say 22 / 8 = 2.8 — inflating the headline and understating every
distance derived from it (page 16 read 0.2 levels behind regional leaders
where the truth is 0.4).
WHAT THIS FIXTURE STILL DOES NOT MIRROR, and it is a source defect, not a
fixture one: MaturityAssessment.tsx hardcodes its own nine-entry CATEGORIES
array and passes `totalCategories: CATEGORIES.length` = 9, with a ninth
radarData row of 0 / 0 / 0 because no question carries that category. So on
the real screen answeredCategories is 8 and totalCategories is 9 — meaning
isDraft is TRUE for every complete BAIW assessment, and the scorecard carries
a 0.0 row. Fixing that is a source change to CATEGORIES in both
pages/MaturityAssessment.tsx and utils/reportGenerator.ts. Until then this
fixture agrees with the screen on the cover score and on all eight measured
rows, and differs only by the phantom.
engagementId/generatedAt/layer were added in D2 step 3, for the same reason
they were added to haiw.json in step 1 and taiw.json in step 2: the PDF and
the markdown now take a ReportMeta, and a clock-derived date would make them
un-reproducible from one day to the next. generatedAt was null before that,
because none of the three BAIW generators accepted one - they called
new Date() directly, and the harness could only normalise the result to a
<DATE> token. The gap CSV reads none of the three - its baseline is
unaffected, and that is checked rather than assumed.
